question.text: The coupon rate of Floating Rate Bonds (FRBs) issued by the Government of India is primarily linked to which benchmark?

explanation.text: The Logic: FRB coupons are majorly linked to the 182-day Treasury Bill rate. The coupon is reset based on the average of implicit cut-off yields of recent 182-day T-Bill auctions, with a fixed spread added. The Trap: Repo rate, 10-year G-Sec yield and MIBOR are also money/bond market reference rates but are not the primary FRB benchmark. Note: Because the coupon is reset with market rates, FRBs' coupon income moves with the benchmark rather than being fixed for the life of the bond.
